title: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The proof, after OpenAI's 2026 manuscript, that every elliptic curve over every imaginary quadratic field K is modular: there is an isobaric automorphic representation of GL_2 over K, of weight zero with trivial central character, whose Galois representations are the cohomology of the curve, with matching local parameters at every place and L(E/K, s) = L(pi_E, s - 1/2). The geometric prime switch: cyclic covers of a quadratic twist branched at two points, integral homology as a module over the group ring, Picard-Lefschetz transvections, congruences between character pieces modulo p, 3 and p, local constancy of reduction types, Hilbert irreducibility for a curve and its conjugate, three applications of the Caraiani-Newton lifting theorem, cyclic descent and the complex multiplication case.
prerequisites: modularity lifting in outline (course Global Langlands, LG-GLOB-11)

Tate modules, Weil-Deligne representations and Grothendieck's monodromy theorem, Frobenius elements and determination by traces, residual representations, the Abel-Jacobi uniformization, p-adic Hodge theory (course Galois representations, LG-GAL)
the rank-two local Langlands correspondence with Steinberg twists (course The local Langlands correspondence, LG-LLC-06)
complex representations of GL_2 and their Whittaker models (course Automorphic forms and representations of GL2)
the Picard-Lefschetz formula at a node (course The Lefschetz trace formula, lesson Lefschetz pencils and vanishing cycles)
the Riemann-Hurwitz formula and the Riemann existence equivalence (course The etale fundamental group)
Hensel's lemma in Newton form (course Local fields, NT-LOC-03)

open_obligations: N1 Caraiani-Newton (arXiv:2301.10509v3): the lifting theorem (Theorem 5.2), the modularity criterion at 5 (Theorem 6.1) and the properties of modular elliptic curves (Lemma 6.1.3), stated as Theorems 4.1-4.3 of lesson 1 and used in lesson 8. Intended home: a course on automorphy lifting over CM fields after LG-GLOB-11.

N2 Galois representations of regular algebraic cuspidal representations of GL_2 over CM fields with local-global compatibility at places not above l (Harris-Lan-Taylor-Thorne, arXiv:1411.6717; Scholze, arXiv:1306.2070, Corollary V.4.2; Varma, arXiv:1411.2520, Theorems 1 and 1^ss), stated as Theorem 2.2 of lesson 1 and used in lesson 8. Intended home: the same course.

N3 Cyclic base change for GL_2 and strong multiplicity one (Langlands, Base change for GL(2), Chapter 2 and Lemma 3.1) and quadratic automorphic induction (Jacquet-Langlands, Proposition 12.1), stated as Theorem 3.1 of lesson 8. Intended home: the course Automorphic forms and representations of GL2 (number-field versions).

N4 Serre's open image theorem (Serre 1972, Section 4.2, Theoreme 2), stated in lesson 5, Theorem 1.1, and used in lessons 5 and 7. Intended home: a lesson on images of Galois representations of elliptic curves in LG-GAL.

N5 Hilbert's irreducibility theorem in the counting form of Cohen and Serre (Zywina, arXiv:1011.6465, Theorem 1.2), stated as Theorem 3.1 of lesson 7; the version with local conditions (Lemma 3.2) is proved from it. Intended home: a lesson on thin sets and Hilbert's irreducibility theorem.

N6 Raynaud's theorem that the identity component of the Neron model represents Pic^0 of the minimal regular model with reduced special fibre (Deligne-Mumford, Section 2, Theorem (2.5)), stated as Theorem 2.5 of lesson 3. Intended home: a lesson on Neron models of Jacobians.

N7 p-adic Hodge theory of abelian varieties: Faltings' Hodge-Tate decomposition (Brinon-Conrad, Theorem 2.2.3), the crystalline and semistable comparison theorems (Berger, Section II.5.1), crystalline Kummer classes (Brinon-Conrad, Lemma 8.3.9; Berger, II.4.4), weak admissibility and the Colmez-Fontaine theorem (Brinon-Conrad, Theorem 9.3.4 and Section 9.3), Dieudonne-Manin (Brinon-Conrad, Theorem 8.1.4), and the Katz-Messing comparison of Frobenius polynomials (Katz-Messing, Theorem 1). Stated in lesson 5, Theorem 3.2, and lesson 6, Theorem 4.2. Intended home: the course on p-adic Hodge theory listed as LG-PADIC in the building list.

N8 Grothendieck's theory of semistable abelian varieties (SGA 7 IX, surveyed by Illusie, Grothendieck and vanishing cycles, Sections 3 and 4) and Raynaud's uniformization (Fresnel-van der Put 1989), stated as Theorem 2.1 of lesson 6. Intended home: the same p-adic course or a course on Neron models.

N9 The main theorem of complex multiplication in the form of algebraic Hecke characters (Milne, Complex Multiplication, Theorem 10.1), stated as Theorem 4.1 of lesson 8. Intended home: a course on complex multiplication.

N10 Abelian varieties: integrality and l-independence of characteristic polynomials, Weil pairings, Neron's criterion and good reduction of Jacobians, Weil's theorem over finite fields, relative Jacobians (Milne, Abelian Varieties, I.10.9, I.10.20, I.13.2, I.17.3, II.1.1, III.8.1, IV.3.5, IV.4.1). Stated in lesson 5, Theorem 3.1, and lesson 6, Theorem 2.2. Intended home: the course on abelian varieties (AG-GS).
